topLine: Coal dominated NSW politics today: the Sydney Morning Herald reports Premier Chris Minns held a fundraiser five days before a mine expansion approval, while the Guardian reports barrister Geoffrey Watson and other legal experts have attacked the government's move on a Hunter Valley coalmine as contrary to the separation of powers. The government also launched its Future Jobs and Investment Authority for coal-producing regions and passed Australia-first 'human composting' laws. Locally, Kiama Municipal Council says it will consult residents before settling how it resolves its finances under the state's Performance Improvement Order.

briefing.topLine: Coal dominated NSW politics today: the Sydney Morning Herald reports Premier Chris Minns held a fundraiser five days before a mine expansion approval, while the Guardian reports barrister Geoffrey Watson and other legal experts have attacked the government's move on a Hunter Valley coalmine as contrary to the separation of powers. The government also launched its Future Jobs and Investment Authority for coal-producing regions and passed Australia-first 'human composting' laws. Locally, Kiama Municipal Council says it will consult residents before settling how it resolves its finances under the state's Performance Improvement Order.
briefing.localWatch: Kiama ratepayers get a say before council finalises its response to the NSW Government's Performance Improvement Order, and Shoalhaven Mayor Patricia White has spoken publicly about threats and intimidation directed at female local leaders. Motorists face seven weeks of night works on the Princes Highway at Ulladulla from 25 October.

stories.headline: Council to consult community before deciding financial plan
stories.summary: Kiama Municipal Council says it will seek community feedback before finalising how it resolves its financial situation, as required under the NSW Government's Performance Improvement Order.

stories.headline: Stalked, threatened and abused: the personal toll on our female leaders
stories.summary: The Milton Ulladulla Times reports Shoalhaven Mayor Patricia White has detailed threats made against her and vandalism at her driveway, in a report on how female leaders in the region are responding to escalating abuse.

stories.headline: Public urged to join fight to save army barracks
stories.summary: The Milton Ulladulla Times reports personnel at a historic army base are due to be relocated by the end of the year, and that the public is being urged to join the campaign to save the barracks.

stories.headline: 'Plan ahead': Highway closures and parking changes set to hit central Ulladulla
stories.summary: The Milton Ulladulla Times reports the Princes Highway at Ulladulla faces night closures and 40km/h limits from 25 October, with safety works scheduled to run for seven weeks.

stories.headline: 'Merge earlier': a 'simple' change to relieve M1 Motorway congestion at busy on-ramp
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Transport for NSW is raising the speed limit on the Figtree M1 on-ramp to 100km/h, with new line markings, in a bid to ease congestion.

stories.headline: Gagging, co-ordinated attacks: reality for female MPs
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports a political candidate who says she was targeted with offensive imagery, slurs and a co-ordinated letterbox drop is speaking out about the treatment of female MPs and candidates.

stories.headline: Coal-producing regions to lead the way under NSW Government’s new Future Jobs and Investment Authority
stories.summary: The Minns Government says it has established the Future Jobs Investment Authority, which it describes as delivering on an election commitment to give certainty to workers and communities in coal-producing regions.

stories.headline: ‘Human composting’ laws pass parliament in Australian first
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports NSW parliament has passed laws legalising terramation, in what it describes as an Australian first, with several MPs saying they would want their own bodies turned into soil after death.

stories.headline: Nearly 300 GPs trained to safely diagnose and treat ADHD
stories.summary: The NSW Government says almost 300 GPs across the state have finished training to diagnose and treat ADHD under reforms it says will make the care more accessible and potentially save families money.

stories.headline: ‘Disgraceful’: Geoffrey Watson accuses Minns government of overturning high court ruling on coalmine
stories.summary: The Guardian reports barrister Geoffrey Watson has used the word "disgraceful" in accusing the Minns government of overturning a High Court ruling in relation to a Hunter Valley coalmine. The report says leading legal experts consider the government's bid to allow the expansion contrary to the separation of powers.

stories.headline: Media sent emails from ALP boss urging ministers to apply for grants
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports it has been sent emails from an ALP official urging ministers to apply for grants. No further detail was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: A city for 5am cafe-goers and after-dark night owls: how CBD could change under this new plan
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Wollongong City Council is considering establishing a Special Entertainment Precinct in the city centre.

stories.headline: Five days before approving mine expansion, Minns held an intimate fundraiser
stories.summary: The Herald reports Premier Chris Minns held a small fundraiser five days before a mine expansion was approved, and argues NSW governments have for years seen value in an independent assessment framework for major mining projects so that such decisions sit outside politicians' hands.

stories.headline: ‘Coal hard truth’ – Governments need to face reality
stories.summary: 2GB's Michael McLaren argues governments should confront what he calls the "coal-hard truth" about coal's importance, and urges the Minns government to rethink its emphasis on Scope 3 emissions, saying Australia should stay practical about its energy position.

stories.headline: We had a rule when I was an editor. It's out the window now in the era of outrage
stories.summary: Writing in the South Coast Register, a former editor reflects on the assault at independent MP Helen Haines's Wangaratta office and argues social media algorithms and outrage are fuelling political hostility.

elsewhere.text: Crikey reports a 43-year-old man has been charged after independent federal MP Helen Haines was hit by a car outside her electorate office, with a court appearance listed.
